nodes.description: A distinct presynaptic lesion in which the nerve terminal itself is built wrongly, rather than the acetylcholine cycle or the fusion machinery failing within an otherwise normal terminal. MYO9A, an unconventional myosin with a Rho GTPase-activating domain, regulates intracellular transport in peripheral nerve; SLC25A1 is a mitochondrial inner-membrane transporter. Knockdown of either in zebrafish disturbs the elongation and branching of spinal motor axons and compromises neuromuscular junction formation, so the myasthenia in CMS23 and CMS24 is attributed to defective nerve terminal development. Cholinesterase inhibitors are effective in MYO9A-CMS, whereas both cholinesterase inhibitors and amifampridine are generally ineffective in SLC25A1-CMS.

nodes.description: Calcium entering the motor nerve terminal through the P/Q-type calcium channel binds the two C2B domains of synaptotagmin-2 and triggers assembly of the SNARE complex - SNAP25, syntaxin and the vesicle SNARE synaptobrevin-1 (VAMP1) - which fuses acetylcholine-laden synaptic vesicles with the presynaptic membrane. Variants in SYT2 or VAMP1 break that calcium-to-fusion coupling, so fewer quanta are released per nerve impulse. The result is a Lambert-Eaton-like electrophysiology, with a decrement on low-frequency repetitive nerve stimulation and an increment at high frequency, which is why amifampridine, which enhances calcium entry into the nerve terminal, is effective in this group. This node is distinct from the upstream acetylcholine synthesis and vesicle-loading defects: here the vesicles are filled, but they do not fuse on cue.

biological_processes: Acetylcholine secretion at the nerve terminal

nodes.description: In synaptic (basal-lamina) CMS, loss of COLQ removes the collagen tail that anchors acetylcholinesterase in the synaptic cleft. The resulting endplate AChE deficiency prolongs ACh dwell time, causing cationic overload and depolarization block / endplate myopathy. Because residual AChE activity is already absent, cholinesterase inhibitors provide no benefit and may be harmful.

nodes.description: Collagen XIII is a single-pass transmembrane collagen enriched at the neuromuscular junction that is required for the maturation and maintenance of endplate acetylcholine receptors. Biallelic COL13A1 variants reduce AChR clustering, and Col13a1-deficient mice form the junction abnormally. The mechanism therefore sits in the synaptic compartment alongside the COLQ lesion but is not an acetylcholinesterase-anchoring defect, which is why the two synaptic subtypes differ in their drug response: cholinesterase inhibitors are contraindicated in COLQ-CMS and merely ineffective in COL13A1-CMS, while salbutamol is reported to help in both.

nodes.description: The shared terminal mechanism of all CMS subtypes. A defect in any component of the motor endplate — presynaptic ACh handling, synaptic AChE anchoring, postsynaptic AChR density/kinetics, AChR clustering, or NMJ glycoprotein glycosylation — reduces the safety factor of cholinergic synaptic transmission. The endplate potential generated by ACh release becomes insufficient to consistently trigger a postsynaptic muscle fiber action potential, and this insufficiency worsens with repetitive activity, producing fatigable weakness.

nodes.description: The largest mechanistic group. Variants in AChR subunit genes (CHRNE, CHRNA1, CHRNB1, CHRND) reduce endplate AChR density (primary AChR deficiency) or alter channel gating kinetics — prolonged openings in slow-channel CMS (cationic overload, endplate degeneration) or abbreviated openings in fast-channel CMS (reduced response to ACh). Variants in the agrin-LRP4-MuSK-DOK7-rapsyn signaling axis (AGRN, LRP4, MUSK, DOK7, RAPSN) impair AChR clustering and endplate development/maintenance.

nodes.description: The acetylcholine-handling arm of presynaptic CMS: the lesion lies in the supply of transmitter rather than in the release machinery. Choline acetyltransferase (CHAT) synthesizes ACh, the high-affinity choline transporter (SLC5A7) recovers choline into the terminal, the vesicular ACh transporter (SLC18A3) loads it into synaptic vesicles, and PREPL is required for those vesicles to be refilled. A defect at any of these steps lowers the quantal content of ACh release and so the endplate potential. In this group a decrement on low-frequency stimulation is elicited at rest in some patients, but only after exercise or high-frequency stimulation in the others. The downstream fusion step is modeled separately in Defective SNARE-Mediated Synaptic Vesicle Fusion, and terminal development in Defective Motor Nerve Terminal Formation.
